cf.title: Fix the wrong behavior of REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY

input.subject: Two issues with REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal: the thread agrees that the concurrent refresh can leave a view that differs from its query. The two surviving objections, maintenance-fit-1 and maintenance-fit-2, are fixable design points. The header comment still states the wrong invariant, and the patch has not been compared with the explicit NULL check from message #21. Confidence is medium because only 3 of 22 messages and the first patch's prose were visible.

brief.title: Detect duplicate rows with NULLs in refresh materialized view concurrently
brief.problem: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY misses duplicate rows that contain a NULL outside the unique-index columns, so the view silently keeps one row where the query returns two. A plain REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW fails on the same data. Users of matviews with nullable columns get a view that no longer matches its query.
brief.proposed_design: The latest bug-1 patch changes the duplicate pre-check in refresh_by_match_merge() to use the per-column equality operators of the unique-index columns plus *=, the same conditions as the FULL OUTER JOIN. Rows that are NULL in an indexed column stay distinct, so they still refresh. A separate patch (CF 6580) for the slow refresh with a unique index on a NULL column is now judged not to work.
user_visible_surface: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY now fails with "new data for materialized view ... contains duplicate rows" for duplicates with NULLs in non-indexed columns.
An alternative patch by ChangAo Chen adds a built-in function record_image_eq_variant; the main patch does not.
author_claims: The fixed pre-check catches (test, NULL) twice with a unique index on a, and still accepts (NULL, NULL) twice.
A unique index on a column of all NULLs makes the refresh 3 to 5 times slower; the bug-2 patch does not fix it.
The bug-1 patch passes the regression tests, and Surya says v7-0001 is ready.
The record_image_eq_variant approach forces a delete and insert for every unchanged row with a NULL in any column.
brief.thread_state: Robert Haas and Yugo Nagata agree it is a bug but want the function header comment, which states the wrong invariant, rewritten. Yugo says the commit message wrongly claims the (NULL, NULL) case as a fix, and asks why the patch uses equality operators over explicit NULL checks; no reply since July 31.
unclear: Which patch version CF 6579 now tracks; the only patch prose shown is Rafia's first 0001.
Whether the fix will be back-patched, and whether a new error in a minor release is acceptable to users.
Whether Robert's simpler fix, checking for NULLs only in unique-index columns, was tried or compared.
The extra cost of the new pre-check on large views.

objections.title: Fix leaves the documented invariant of refresh_by_match_merge() wrong
objections.failure_scenario: A later developer works on the issue 2 slowdown or another change to the diff join and trusts the header comment saying the join is correct for any row with a NULL. They change which key columns enter the join or the pre-check. Duplicates with NULLs outside key columns get through again, and no test or message catches it until a user reports a stale view.
objections.argument: In message #21 Robert Haas says the header comment is wrong in two ways and that the fix should update it. In message #22 Yugo Nagata asks for the comment to explain why the NULL-in-key-column case works. The only patch prose shown, and v7-0001 as described, leave that comment as it is. The correctness of this code rests on a subtle interaction between *= and per-column equality, so the comment is the main defence against regressions here.
objections.author_must_show: Can the next version rewrite the header comment to state the real invariant, NULLs in unique-index columns only, and say why the join is then correct?

critic.reasoning: Robert Haas says in message #21 that the fix does not touch the header comment and that its last sentence states the wrong invariant. Yugo Nagata agrees in message #22, and no later version or reply addresses it.

objections.title: Pre-check mechanism chosen without comparing it to explicit NULL checks
objections.failure_scenario: After a minor release, a site with a large concurrently refreshed matview whose rows often hold NULLs in non-key columns finds the refresh slower. Those rows were skipped by the old IS NOT NULL filter but now enter the EXISTS self-join on newdata. Nobody measured this before the release.
objections.argument: Robert Haas (message #21) suggested a narrower change that checks only for NULLs in unique-index columns. Yugo Nagata (message #22) asked why the patch uses equality operators instead of explicit NULL checks, and the thread has no answer. The thread shows no timing for the new pre-check on large views, only regression-test passes (message #20). A back-patched bug fix should pick the variant that is easiest to reason about and show what it costs.
objections.author_must_show: How does the equality-operator pre-check compare with Robert's explicit NULL check in clarity and in refresh time on a large view with many NULLs in non-key columns?

critic.reasoning: Message #17 says the pre-check mirrors the join operators, but Yugo's later question in #22 has no reply and no pre-check timing is shown. Any correct fix must scan rows with NULLs in non-key columns, so that cost does not favour either variant.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: A back-patched fix makes some concurrent refreshes that succeed today fail with the duplicate-rows error after a minor upgrade.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The header comment of refresh_by_match_merge() states an invariant that the fix shows to be wrong, and the patch leaves it unchanged.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The changed pre-check runs on every concurrent refresh and now includes rows with NULLs; the thread shows no timing.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Can the next version rewrite the header comment of refresh_by_match_merge() to state the real invariant and explain why the join is correct for NULLs in unique-index columns?
Why does the pre-check use the per-column equality operators instead of the explicit NULL check on unique-index columns suggested in message #21?
How long does the new pre-check take on a large view with many NULLs in non-indexed columns, compared with the current code?
Is the fix meant for back-patching, and if so, what should the release note tell users whose refreshes will start to fail?
Which patch version does CommitFest entry 6579 track now, and does its commit message still claim the (NULL, NULL) case as a fix?

committability.owner_note: Robert Haas reviewed the fix in message #21 and asked for the header comment to be rewritten; the owner needs to know the matview diff join and row comparison operators.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the correctness of the duplicate pre-check in all supported branches if back-patched, and for refreshes that start to fail after a minor upgrade.
committability.author_follow_up: The authors posted versions up to v7, but Yugo Nagata's questions in message #22 have had no reply since July 31.

priority.reason: This is a wrong-result fix in one function of matview.c with no new user-visible surface, and reviewers agree it is a bug. It needs a new version that answers messages #21 and #22 before a committer can take it.

provisional_note: The code and the later patch versions were not read, so the exact pre-check query, its schema qualification of operators and its cost could not be checked. Only 3 of 22 messages were visible in full.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add statistics refresh materialized view
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add per-view statistics for REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW (execution count and last refresh time) to the statistics collector, exposed as new columns in pg_stat_all_tables and its user/sys variants. The aim was to record when and how often each materialized view was refreshed without relying on pg_stat_statements.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Fujii Masao objected that adding columns to pg_stat_all_tables for one utility command is a poor design: it singles out REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW over commands such as TRUNCATE or CLUSTER, would lead to many per-command columns, and the columns would be useless for most entries, which are tables. He also suggested that pg_stat_statements and log_statement could already provide the information per view. The author agreed that these tools may be sufficient for most use cases and withdrew the proposal, and the entry was marked Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's not good design to add new columns per utility command into
pg_stat_all_tables. Otherwise pg_stat_all_tables will have to have lots of
columns to expose the stats of many utility commands at last.

precedents_retrieved.title: EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW
precedents_retrieved.summary: Allow EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE on REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, showing the plan of the view's defining SELECT (plain EXPLAIN without refreshing, EXPLAIN ANALYZE performing the refresh), analogous to existing EXPLAIN support for CREATE TABLE AS / CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW. A companion patch refactored ExecRefreshMatView into smaller functions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that supporting EXPLAIN would bind REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW to having an explainable SQL plan, constraining future implementations such as incremental view maintenance, while offering little beyond explaining the view's query directly; the author agreed to withdraw the feature. The leftover refactoring patch was also not taken, because John Naylor judged it would conflict with the refactoring in the pending incremental view maintenance patch without helping it.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The problem with it is that it
binds us to the assumption that REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW has an
explainable plan.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix for REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW ownership error message
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW so that a permission failure reports "must be owner of materialized view" instead of the generic "must be owner of relation", by passing OBJECT_MATVIEW to the ACL check error path. The author offered to prepare back-patches for released branches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers considered the change cosmetic and argued against back-patching: the existing message is not wrong, and changing behavior in released branches can affect applications that depend on the current text. While writing a regression test, the author found that HEAD/v11 already produced the correct message because of an earlier commit. With no back-patch planned, nothing was left to fix, and the author withdrew the patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow granting of permission to REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, CLUSTER, and REINDEX
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, CLUSTER and REINDEX grantable to non-owners, instead of being limited to the table owner, by changing the shared permission check RangeVarCallbackOwnsTable(). The preliminary patch reused the TRUNCATE privilege as a proof of concept; the intended design was a single new table privilege (e.g. REFRESH) covering all three operations.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected to spending one of the four free AclMode privilege bits on this, to reusing TRUNCATE, and to the backward-compatibility effect on existing owner ACLs after upgrade. The discussion then turned to how to extend the privilege-bit space (widening AclMode to 64 bits, a varlena aclitem, or a larger fixed-size aclitem) and whether to use one MAINTAIN privilege or finer-grained ones, without reaching agreement. The CommitFest manager noted no activity over two commitfests and that the thread agreed only that the problem of adding privileges extensibly had to be solved first; after no response, the entry was returned with feedback.

So I can't see using one of them up for
REFRESH, let alone using three of them up for REFRESH, CLUSTER and

precedents_retrieved.title: Apply worker fails if a relation is missing on subscriber even if refresh publication has not been refreshed yet
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch would let the logical replication apply worker skip changes for tables that were added to a publication but are not yet in pg_subscription_rel on the subscriber, because ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH PUBLICATION has not been run. It would log a warning instead of failing repeatedly when such a table is missing on the subscriber.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila questioned whether the current ERROR behavior should be changed when no specific use case had been given. He noted that users can avoid the failure loop with the disable_on_error subscription parameter, and that silently skipping changes could surprise users whose subscriber-side setup is incomplete. The author said he had no specific use case, and the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I see your point but not sure if it is worth changing the
current behavior without any specific use case which we want to
address with this change.

precedents_retrieved.title: Incremental Materialized View Maintenance
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add incremental materialized views (CREATE INCREMENTAL MATERIALIZED VIEW) that Postgres keeps current in the same transaction as base table changes, using AFTER triggers and transition tables. The patch computes deltas from the view definition and applies them to the view, with support for joins, some built-in aggregates, EXISTS subqueries and outer joins.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier marked the entry Returned with Feedback after a month with no update. In July 2022 huyajun had reported bugs: a deadlock between TRUNCATE and concurrent INSERT, wrong counts after concurrent DELETEs, crashes on mismatched column lists, and an unwanted unique index on cross joins. The author said he was still working on them. Paquier also noted little design discussion in three years, and Greg Stark had earlier called the patch hard to review.

precedents_retrieved.title: psql: add \si, \sm, \st and \sr functions to show CREATE commands for indexes, matviews, triggers and tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds psql commands \si, \sm, \st and \sr that show the CREATE command for indexes, materialized views, triggers and tables, modelled on the existing \sf and \sv. Indexes and triggers use pg_get_triggerdef() and pg_indexes.indexdef, while psql rebuilds table and materialized view DDL itself with its own client-side queries.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the output must be fully correct DDL, so psql would need a second copy of pg_dump's large and often-changing DDL logic. He said a shared library built from pg_dump's code should come first. He also noted that the patch fails on older servers, which describe.c must support, and that the commands need review against CVE-2018-1058-style search_path attacks. The author did not respond, and the entry was marked returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I can't accept that we want another copy in psql --- especially one that looks nothing like what pg_dump has.

precedents_retrieved.title: Remove useless GROUP BY columns considering unique index
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets remove_useless_groupby_columns use unique constraints whose columns are all NOT NULL, in addition to the primary key, to drop functionally dependent GROUP BY columns. When several candidates exist, it picks the one with the fewest columns so that the most columns can be removed.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch no longer applied because it relied on catalogued NOT NULL constraints, which had been removed. David Rowley also objected to choosing the constraint with the fewest columns, which ignores column width and can pick a constraint with no columns in the GROUP BY clause, a regression against today's primary-key behaviour. The author said he would study the advice and update, but the visible messages show no new version before the entry was returned.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It looks like it  won't work if the UNIQUE constraint with
the least columns gets no mention in the GROUP BY clause. That'll
cause performance regressions from what we have today when the primary
key is mentioned and columns can be removed using that but a UNIQUE
constraint exists which has no corresponding GROUP BY columns and
fewer unique columns than the PK.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. The only listed precedent, P3, covers a cosmetic REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW error-message change and its back-patch policy, not duplicate detection in the concurrent refresh. The thread cites no earlier attempt at this fix, so the prior-attempts angle has nothing to raise.

The visible contract changes in one way: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY now raises the existing "contains duplicate rows" error for duplicates with NULLs in non-key columns. That matches what plain REFRESH already does on the same data, and the old result was a view that silently differed from its query. The fix adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object or pg_dump change. A back-patch would make some scheduled refreshes start failing after a minor upgrade, but the failure replaces silent wrong data, so it needs a release note rather than an objection. The record_image_eq_variant function is only in the alternative patch.

The bug-1 patch only changes the duplicate pre-check query in refresh_by_match_merge(). It adds no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog entry, protocol message or extension API, and the refresh still writes through ordinary WAL-logged DML. ChangAo Chen's alternative adds a built-in function, which needs a catversion bump and cannot be back-patched, but the main patch does not take that route.

The proposal has no new privilege or exposure aspect. It changes only the duplicate pre-check query, which runs inside REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY for a user who already owns the view or holds MAINTAIN. It uses the same per-column equality operators that the existing FULL OUTER JOIN already uses, and the existing duplicate-rows error with its row DETAIL. Not checked without the code: that the new operator references are schema-qualified like the existing ones.

The fix stays inside one function and adds no GUC, catalog or API, so it carries little long-term cost. Two committers agree it is a bug. The objections above concern how the fix is documented and justified, not whether it belongs in core.

This is a correctness fix inside refresh_by_match_merge(), where REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY can leave a view that no longer matches its query. No existing option or extension makes the concurrent refresh detect these duplicates. Plain REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW avoids the bug but takes an exclusive lock, so it does not meet the same need. Precedent [P3] concerned a cosmetic error message and does not apply.

This is a wrong-result bugfix. Two committers in messages #21 and #22 agree the matview can silently diverge from its query, so demand needs no further proof. The open questions are the header comment and the choice of equality operators versus explicit NULL checks, which are design points for other angles.
